title: Baby head ultrasound
what: The doctor uses ultrasound to look at your baby's brain through the soft spot on the head. It is safe and does not hurt.
why: Often as a routine check in the first months. Also for babies born early, after a difficult birth, or if the doctor is worried about something.
tell_doctor: If your baby was born early
What worries you: spitting up, startling, or restless sleep

prepare.title: Age
prepare.text: It is done while the soft spot is still open, usually until age 1. It shows best in the first months.

prepare.title: Feeding
prepare.text: It helps to feed your baby shortly before the scan. A full baby is calmer and often falls asleep.

prepare.title: Special preparation
prepare.text: None is needed. You do not need to wash your baby's hair beforehand.

bring: A baby blanket or changing sheet
Past reports, if you have them
steps: Your baby is laid on a blanket on the exam table. The hair does not need to be moved aside
Mom or dad stays close, holds the baby, and soothes them
A little gel is put on the soft spot
The doctor gently places the probe and changes its angle
Sometimes other soft spots or the temple are used too
feel: It does not hurt your baby. The probe barely presses
Your baby may fuss because of the cool gel or being held
after: The gel is wiped off with a tissue
You can feed your baby and go out right away
You usually get the report right away. Your pediatrician or neurologist will review it

faq.q: Is a head ultrasound harmful for a baby?
faq.a: No. It is ultrasound with no radiation, and it can be repeated as often as needed.

faq.q: Why does my 1-month-old need a head ultrasound?
faq.a: It is a common routine check. While the soft spot is open, the brain is easy to see, and the doctor can spot changes in time.
